it is a term from the vernacular of India; in the language of Tang (Chinese), it means "Golden-Winged Bird. It does not, however, refer to the exact same entity [as the mythical bird].
This is its name;
it is a translation based on the combination of meanings (huiyi).
Nevertheless, these scriptures and treatises have been transmitted for a long time throughout the ages.
Now, the virtue of the dragon is hidden and subtle, its transformations being limitless.
To oppose it brings disaster;
to honor it summons blessings.
Exhaustively investigating their modes of birth,
they possess the four types— womb-born, egg-born, moisture-born, and transformation-born—
and are free from any further afflictions.
There are only four types of *garuḍas* and *nāgas* who are born from eggs;
birds are likewise of four kinds.
Among these, the birds born by transformation (*upapāduka*) possess the power to subdue the others.
A moisture-born dragon lacks the power to subdue a womb-born bird;
this serves as an analogy to clarify the point.
Furthermore, the vast ocean has no shore.
As the dragons swim and frolic,
they flap their wings and feathers,
fanning up the waves until the waters run dry.
The dragon has no head and indulges its appetite at will,
having no leisure to attain peace.
The reason for this is that its bird-like form is hunched and bent.
First, because they are restrained by the prohibitions of the Dharma,
their physical substance differs from that of ordinary people;
how could their thoughts be any different?
At the moment of descending, focus intently on earth, water, fire, wind, and space; likewise, by reversing and interchanging their applications,
even dragons can be subdued—
how much more so others?
Furthermore, among those honored in the world, Brahmā occupies the foremost place;
Viṣṇu is second;
and Mahādeva is third.
The refuge upon which the ten thousand deities rely;
that which the four modes of birth look up to;
endowed with a heart of compassion and pity.
He performed the Dharma for deliverance;
as a garuḍa among the animals of the air,
he subdued the feathered tribes in such a manner that they relied upon him to further cultivate their practice.
He was able to save the world,
and thus he was named after the *garuḍa*.
He expounded one hundred thousand verses of the scriptural teachings.
Lord of the three realms,
deity of the five great elements,
who has fully realized the true body.
Both traditions transmit the original sounds;
the Dragon King receives his commands,
and the Lord of Devas fears his majesty.
How could a bird be capable of this?
It is rather the power of the Sage.
Now, I shall briefly describe the sublime gate of the Garuḍa.
Next, the miscellaneous rites for the various devas are explained.

It is further taught that this body is composed of the deities of the five great elements—earth, water, fire, wind, and space—and each of these has its respective function.
First, regarding the *karmakāra-garuḍa-mudrā*: with both hands hollowed and joined in *añjali*, interlace the fingers; by pressing the left over the right at the tips, the seal is formed.
This mudrā can accomplish all tasks;
it is the foremost of all mudrās and is able to give rise to all other mudrās.
Whenever one wishes to form a ritual bond (*saṃdhi*), it is first appropriate to perform this. 2.
The Beak Seal of the Garuḍa (Garuḍamukhamudrā), second: With both hands, bend the thumbs and little fingers; press the left over the right and insert them into the palms.
The remaining six fingers are each placed side by side and joined together like the beak of a bird;
when the wrists are thus joined, the Kara-mudrā is formed.
Third, the Kara-mudrā of the Garuḍa: the palm of the left hand faces outward.
Slightly bending the tips of the five fingers, it is thus formed.
4. The Sāpaka-garuḍa Seal (The Fourth): "Sāpa Seal. In Chinese, this is called the "Snake Seal. With the palms joined hollowly:
Bend the two index fingers so their backs touch each other,
and press them down together with the thumbs.
The two little fingers are likewise like the index fingers;
the middle and ring fingers are separated by more than one cun,
resembling the mouth of a snake.

5. The Maṅkāra Seal of the Garuḍa (Maṅkāramudrā-garuḍa). The fifth, the Maṅkāra Seal—translated into Chinese as the "Seal of the Leviathan" (Jingyu yin)—is formed by placing the ring finger of the right hand between the little finger and the index finger of the left hand.
Place the left ring finger between the right ring finger and middle finger.
Hook the tip of the right index finger with the left index finger,
and hook the tip of the left index finger with the right index finger.
The sixth is the *Pakṣa* Seal (Garuḍa *Pakṣa* Seal). Join the two middle fingers and the two little fingers together and side by side;
press the two thumbs against the sides of the middle fingers, and it is formed.
[The *Pakṣa* Seal] is translated into Chinese as the "Golden-Winged Bird Seal" (*Jinshiwu Yin*). Cross the two thumbs, with the left pressing down upon the right.
With the back of the hand facing upward and the remaining fingers extended,
one fans with the eight fingers pointing upward; thus it is accomplished.
7. The Heart-Seal of Garuḍa, the Seventh: With the left hand, place the three fingers at the head [of the right hand] and grasp the right little finger;
with the three fingers of the right hand, encircle the left little finger.
Place each thumb over the side of its respective index finger;
first open the mudrā so that the thumbs are separated by approximately three inches.
Then, gradually applying force, one should grasp the two little fingers.
Next, join the wrists so that the two thumbs are aligned side by side as a standard.
When applying force to grasp them:
The body of the spirit causing this illness is no different from my own little finger;
I shall now subdue it,
and that spirit shall be bound.
If a patient speaks in the language of ghosts, seeking compassion and pleading for their life,
one should ask them the reason for this and instruct them to grant pardon;
the illness will then be cured.
If one suffers from minor ailments, the venom of snakes, poisonous drugs, or diseases caused by malevolent spells,
one should apply this seal according to the previous instructions;
furthermore, one may also fixate upon the various limbs and joints as desired.

First, one should extensively and perfectly manifest it within one's own body,
maintaining one's own form as that of the King of Garuḍas.
If one does not perform this visualization of forming the body, [the practice will not succeed].
It is sufficient merely to bind the Maṅkara mudrā to protect oneself.
Furthermore, those who receive the poison will have their bodies become vast and expansive.
Then, one should visualize the character *cha* (姹),
white like crystal, encircling that person;
it branches out to separate the joints and the heart, preventing the poison from passing through.
If one does not perform this visualization,
one should instead form the Maṅgalamudrā and seal the joints of the limbs.
Recite the mantra for subduing poison three times;
one may even ingest poison.
Then, take aconite or other poisons and hold them without biting them.
Empower the medicine seven times with the mantra.
At the time of empowerment,
bring the medicine close to the mouth.
Continue to rotate it several times without ceasing;
you should place it in the hands of the person before you.
If they were to release poison from their feet, [it would be neutralized].
One then places that person beneath one's feet.
The practitioner raises the palm of the right hand, slightly bending it,
with the four fingers extended straight.
With the thumbs forming the two combined syllables held in the palms like a mass of fire,
one should visualize the fire gradually intensifying.
A stream of blazing flames issued forth and struck the place where the person was fixed in concentration;
the poison remained within the medicine and emitted a powerful vapor.
Just like blue smoke,
it enters his body and reaches the place where he is bound, remaining there accordingly.
When the smoke enters, recite the syllable *kha* continuously and secretly;
then, according to one's will, direct it to wherever the poison has reached,
and it will suddenly become as if the victim were struck by a wind-ailment (*vāta*).
This is its sign.
Within a brief moment, the color of the flesh turns blue.
If it is released from the entire body, [the same occurs].
Simply cause the character *chù* (姹) to encircle the person's heart;
then, even if poison is released to pervade the entire body, it shall not reach the heart.
Treat this according to the method for collecting all poisons.
If it is not extracted,
the poison will not be cured,
yet the person will not die either.

even if it is removed,

they would simply cycle through them again and again.

VĀPAYA SVĀHĀ. If one wishes to cure all poisons,
one should first visualize oneself as being exactly like the King of Garuḍas,
vast and perfectly complete.
Furthermore, while maintaining awareness of the patient's physical form,
one should contemplate the five great elements (mahābhūta) as being vast and capable of containing all;
then, one should visualize empty space.
Then, one should visualize a black circular mandala that is boundless,
positioned above the forehead of the patient,
with the syllable *Ha* in its center.
Furthermore, visualize the fire element as a blazing flame in the shape of a triangle at the heart,
with the syllable Oṃ situated in its center.
Again, one visualizes the water element as being shaped like a half-moon,
green in color, and located at one's navel.
Place the syllable BA in the center.
Furthermore, visualize the wind element as a yellow circle at both knees.
Within the *svāhā* [syllable],
the earth element is square and white,
located in the portion of the feet.
The syllable *khāḥ* is at the tip of the thumb of the left hand;
the syllable *vaṃ*, representing the element water, is on the index finger;
and the syllable *oṃ*, representing the element fire, is on the middle finger.
The wind element, *svā*, is on the ring finger.
The space contemplation, the syllable *ha*, is at the tip of the little finger.
First, close your eyes and single-mindedly maintain these.
However, using the secret mantras of the aforementioned five great devas,

With the palms facing outward at a distance of five inches from the patient’s body,

Furthermore, maintain the visualization of the black letter *Ha* in the space between that person’s eyebrows within the void;
as you follow the mudrā downward, expel and eliminate the poison.

The deity has three heads, eight eyes, and two arms;
flames arise from his entire body.

This transcription of the *Kāraṇḍavyūha Sūtra* (Holding the Mantra Sūtra) by the Garuḍa King was completed on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month in the third year of the Kenpō era at the residence on the western mountain of Kanzeon-ji. On the twenty-ninth, it was transcribed again using the original manuscript.
